idiom_name: NestJS transporter ClientProxy/@MessagePattern, or a typed interface over amqplib/kafkajs
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds a declared interface on the application side while the transport work is delegated: NestJS abstracts each transporter behind a canonical interface, with ClientProxy.send/emit on the outbound side and @MessagePattern/@EventPattern handlers on the inbound side, and KafkaJS's producer.send / consumer.run({ eachMessage }) is the raw client behind it. Either way the adapter maps domain types to serialized payloads (`JSON.stringify`/`Buffer`/`ByteBuffer`) so no transport type appears in application signatures; use generics for the payload contract instead of annotating broker types. NestJS makes the adapter mostly configuration (ClientsModule.register) plus one handler class per pattern.
pitfalls: @MessagePattern handlers are discovered by class metadata and receive untyped payloads at runtime, so the compile-time contract is lost exactly at the seam unless each handler validates or types its argument.
KafkaJS consumer.run resolves once the consumer joins the group rather than when processing ends: startup code that awaits it never continues, so readiness must be signalled from eachMessage.
ClientProxy connections are lazy (connect() is only called on first send), which hides misconfiguration until the first message; call connect() during bootstrap when failure should be early.
